html:
The Salar de Uyuni is the world's largest salt flat, about 10,000 square kilometres of white crust high in southwestern Bolivia. Beneath it lies one of the world's largest deposits of lithium.

It is the remains of ancient lakes that dried out. For centuries local people cut salt there and traded it by llama caravan. Its flat mirror-like surface draws many tourists, and satellites use it to calibrate their instruments.

Lithium, needed for batteries in phones and electric cars, made it a prize. From 2008 the government of Evo Morales chose to develop it through a state company rather than foreign firms, but output stayed small. The lithium triangle of Bolivia, Argentina and Chile holds much of the world's supply, and Bolivia hopes it will not repeat the story of silver.
sum: The Salar de Uyuni is the world's largest salt flat, about 10,000 square kilometres of white crust high in southwestern Bolivia. Beneath it lies one of the world's largest deposits of lithium.
